definition: A key idea of cosmic order, duty and right conduct. Its exact content depends on a person's role, age and situation, and different traditions explain it in different ways.

The principle that actions and intentions shape a person's future, in this life or in later ones. Traditions disagree about how literally to read this, and some stress intention as much as outward action.
A form in which a deity descends into the world, most often used of Vishnu's many descents. Lists of avatars vary between texts and communities.
A class of divine being, often translated as god, associated with light, order and the heavens. Devas are powerful but not necessarily all-powerful or eternal.
A class of powerful divine beings often shown in rivalry with the devas. They are not simply equivalent to evil, and individual asuras may be wise, devout or heroic.
The nectar of immortality that emerges from the churning of the ocean. In some tellings it is a drink; in others it stands for a state beyond death.
Release from the cycle of birth and death, the final goal for many Hindu traditions. Schools differ over what release is like and how it is reached.
Devotion to a deity as a path to liberation, often expressed through song, poetry and ritual. Bhakti movements reshaped the religious life of the subcontinent.
One of the great ages of cosmic time, which are said to follow one another in a repeating cycle. Their lengths and qualities are described differently in different Puranas.
A genre of Sanskrit texts holding creation accounts, genealogies and devotional stories of the gods. There are many Puranas, and they do not always agree with one another.
